belongs_to: 'How many different ways can you divide a square into 4 parts of equal area? ... Consider a division, such as —' (first figure)
description: A square with a plain black outline, no letters, no numbers, no shading. One vertical line and one horizontal line through the centre divide it into 4 equal smaller squares (2 x 2 arrangement). Total 4 parts.

belongs_to: '... and alter each part as follows.' (second figure, the same square with each part altered)
description: The same square (plain black outline, no letters, no numbers, no shading) divided into 4 parts that meet at the centre point. Each of the 4 half-lines that run from the centre to the middle of a side is not straight: the half-line is split into three equal stretches (each about 1/6 of the side) and the middle stretch is replaced by a three-sided rectangular notch whose depth is also about 1/6 of the side. The notches go round like a pinwheel: top half of the vertical line = notch bulges to the LEFT (into the top-left part); right half of the horizontal line = notch bulges UP (into the top-right part); bottom half of the vertical line = notch bulges to the RIGHT (into the bottom-right part); left half of the horizontal line = notch bulges DOWN (into the bottom-left part). So every part has one notch cut out of it and one equal tab added to it, all 4 parts keep equal area. Outer boundary is still a perfect square. 4 notches in total, all the same size.
unclear: exact notch size read as about 1/6 of the side by measuring the picture; the book gives no numbers
